answer: The hypothesis is partially supported: among 50 estimates with confidence intervals, 37 were statistically significant and positive, while 8 were statistically significant and negative and 5 were indeterminate. The evidence is not uniform across outcomes or race-comparison definitions, so it supports racial bias for some specified contrasts rather than the broad claim without qualification.
rationale: Positive significant results are the majority, but the 8 significant negative results and strong decision sensitivity prevent a robustly supported conclusion. Outcome choice produced a 0.52 inference-flip rate and 0.32 sign-reversal rate, while race-comparison choice produced a 0.333 inference-flip rate; the corresponding median standardized effects also differed substantially.
key_evidence: 37 of 50 estimates were statistically significant and positive; 8 were statistically significant and negative; 5 were indeterminate.
The median standardized estimate was 0.00486, with estimates ranging from -0.01455 to 0.02912.
Median effects differed by outcome: 0.000592 for contraband hit rate versus 0.02023 for the combined search-and-hit outcome.
Median effects differed by race comparison: 0.01777 for black versus white, 0.0000143 for all known races, and 0.000104 for including unknown race as a category.
refinement_reason: The broad hypothesis combines distinct outcomes and race-comparison populations whose estimated effects and inferences differ materially.
refinement_dimensions: Primary outcome: search rate versus contraband hit rate
Race comparison: black versus white versus all known or unknown-inclusive categories
suggested_hypotheses: Among the specified population of stops, police search-conducted rates differ positively between black and white subjects.
Among searched stops, contraband hit rates differ positively between black and white subjects under a prespecified hit definition.
Racial differences in stops or searches vary by the selected race-comparison set, and should be tested separately rather than pooled into one broad claim.
caveats: The evidence is on standardized associations or differences and does not by itself establish a causal mechanism.
There were 206 unavailable universes out of 256, although 768 results were reported and 50 estimates had confidence intervals.
The outcome-model and inference choices could not be compared in paired sensitivity analyses: all such comparisons had zero effect pairs.
Non-significant results are not evidence of no racial difference.

geographic_scope.label: Geographic scope of stops
geographic_scope.rationale: Which records should represent the population of police stops being tested for racial bias?  [found by: direct]

all_records.label: All records in the dataset
all_records.description: Include every row with a usable subject_race value, regardless of county_name, location, or department_name.

durham_county.label: Durham County stops
durham_county.description: Keep only rows where county_name equals "Durham County"; retain stops from all departments in that county.

durham_police_department.label: Durham Police Department stops
durham_police_department.description: Keep only rows where department_name equals "Durham Police Department", regardless of county_name.

race_comparison_set.label: Race comparison and coding
race_comparison_set.rationale: Which recorded driver-race groups should be compared?  [found by: direct]

black_vs_white.label: Black versus white comparison
black_vs_white.description: Keep only rows with subject_race equal to "black" or "white"; model or report the black-minus-white difference, with white as the reference group.

all_known_races.label: All known race categories
all_known_races.description: Keep all rows whose subject_race is not "unknown" and estimate separate associations for black, white, hispanic, asian/pacific islander, and other, using white as the reference group.

include_unknown_as_category.label: Include unknown race as a category
include_unknown_as_category.description: Retain all rows, including subject_race equal to "unknown", and treat "unknown" as an additional categorical race level rather than missing data.

bias_outcome.label: Primary observable outcome
bias_outcome.rationale: Which observable consequence of a stop should be treated as the test outcome for racial bias?  [found by: direct]

search_rate.label: Search-conducted rate
search_rate.description: Use search_conducted as a binary outcome for every included stop; estimate the racial difference in the probability of a search.

contraband_hit_rate.label: Contraband hit rate among searches
contraband_hit_rate.description: Restrict to stops with search_conducted equal to 1 and use contraband_found as the binary outcome; estimate racial differences in the probability that a search recovered contraband.

search_and_hit_rates.label: Both search rate and hit rate
search_and_hit_rates.description: Report a search_conducted outcome for all included stops and a separate contraband_found outcome among searched stops, treating both as primary racial-bias tests.

hit_definition.label: Definition of a contraband hit
hit_definition.rationale: When a hit-rate analysis is conducted, what should count as recovered contraband?  [found by: direct]

any_contraband.label: Any contraband
any_contraband.description: Among rows with search_conducted equal to 1, code a hit as contraband_found equal to TRUE and a non-hit as contraband_found equal to FALSE; exclude missing contraband_found values.

drugs_only.label: Drugs only
drugs_only.description: Among rows with search_conducted equal to 1, use contraband_drugs as the binary hit outcome; exclude rows where contraband_drugs is missing.

weapons_only.label: Weapons only
weapons_only.description: Among rows with search_conducted equal to 1, use contraband_weapons as the binary hit outcome; exclude rows where contraband_weapons is missing.

not_applicable.label: Not applicable
not_applicable.description: Do not define a hit outcome because the analysis uses only search_conducted.

time_of_day_adjustment.label: Treatment of stop time
time_of_day_adjustment.rationale: How should date and time be used when comparing racial search or hit outcomes?  [found by: direct]

no_time_adjustment.label: No time adjustment
no_time_adjustment.description: Use date and time only for parsing or descriptive summaries; estimate racial differences without conditioning on date, hour, or daylight status.

clock_time_controls.label: Clock-time and calendar controls
clock_time_controls.description: Include hour-of-day indicators derived from time, plus calendar-year and month indicators derived from date, as adjustment variables in the outcome model.

veil_of_darkness.label: Veil-of-darkness comparison
veil_of_darkness.description: Construct daylight status from date, time, and a specified sunset calculation for the stop location; compare stops near the daylight-to-dark transition while controlling for date or season, rather than using all hours equally.

outcome_model_and_inference.label: Outcome model and uncertainty calculation
outcome_model_and_inference.rationale: How should racial differences be estimated and how should repeated stops or officers affect uncertainty?  [found by: direct]

unadjusted_proportions_iid.label: Unadjusted proportions with independent-stop uncertainty
unadjusted_proportions_iid.description: Estimate group-specific outcome proportions and their differences directly, using a two-sample proportion test or equivalent model with observations treated as independent; do not adjust for subject_age, subject_sex, reason_for_stop, officer_id_hash, or department_name.

adjusted_logistic_officer_clustered.label: Covariate-adjusted logistic regression clustered by officer
adjusted_logistic_officer_clustered.description: Fit a logistic regression for the selected binary outcome with race, subject_age, subject_sex, and reason_for_stop as predictors; include calendar or time variables only if selected separately, and use officer_id_hash-clustered standard errors.

department_and_officer_controls.label: Officer and department controls
department_and_officer_controls.description: Fit a logistic regression including race, subject_age, subject_sex, reason_for_stop, department_name indicators, and officer_id_hash fixed effects, with uncertainty clustered by officer_id_hash; observations from officers with no within-officer race variation cannot identify the race coefficient.
